title: The Prophet's character
hookLine: Aisha said his character was the Qur'an (Muslim)

cards: Tell me about his character. What was he actually like? A man named Sa'd ibn Hisham has come to Aisha, the wife of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, with a list of things he wants to understand, and this is the big one.
He might have expected a story, or a list of virtues. Aisha answers with a question of her own. Don't you read the Qur'an?
Yes, he says. Then, she says, his character was the Qur'an. That short exchange is kept in Sahih Muslim.

teach.h: KHULUQ: THE WAY A PERSON HABITUALLY IS.
teach.b: First, the word. In Arabic it's khuluq: character, disposition, the way a person habitually is.
The same word sits in a verse addressed to the Prophet himself, in Pickthall's translation: "And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature." Nature there is khuluq.

teach.h: SHE HANDED HIM A BOOK, NOT A PORTRAIT.
teach.b: So Aisha's answer points straight back to the book. Second, what her answer does. She doesn't hand Sa'd a portrait; she hands him a text he already owns.
If you want to know the man, read what he lived by: the patience, the honesty, the mercy, the prayer at night.
Some readers take her words in two directions at once: the Qur'an shows what his character was, and his life shows what the Qur'an looks like when a person actually does it.

teach.h: SMALL MOMENTS: HOME, A SERVANT, A SMILE.
teach.b: Third, the small evidence. The hadith collections keep ordinary moments, not only great ones. Asked what he did at home, Aisha said he kept busy serving his family, and when the call to prayer came he went out to pray.
That's in Sahih al-Bukhari. Anas, who served him as a boy for ten years, said he was never once told off with so much as a sigh of annoyance, never asked why did you do that. Bukhari keeps that too.
And a saying in Tirmidhi counts a smile at your brother as charity. Fourth, why it matters on an ordinary afternoon.

teach.h: HABITS ARE SMALL ENOUGH TO COPY.
teach.b: A character is built from habits, and habits are small enough to copy.

teach.h: AND LO! THOU ART OF A TREMENDOUS NATURE.
teach.b: Nobody copies a whole life in a day. But one habit, a smile, a hand with the dishes, holding back the irritated sigh, can be tried before dinner.

how: Muslims learn the Prophet's character from the Qur'an and the hadith collections, and many try to copy his everyday habits, such as smiling, helping at home and speaking gently, as part of following his sunnah.

o: character: the way a person habitually is
the sermon given at the Friday prayer
creation, the act of making the world

games.q: the prophet's character — tap the pairs.
p: character, the way someone habitually is
served him and was never scolded

s: Aisha answered with a long list of his virtues
she answered with a question: don't you read the Qur'an? his character was the Qur'an.
the word for character in Aisha's answer also appears in the Qur'an about him
khuluq: Pickthall renders it "thou art of a tremendous nature."
the hadith collections only keep his great public moments
they keep small ones too: housework, a servant boy, a smile.

games.q: you are Aisha. a man asks you to describe the Prophet's character. what do you say?
o: tell him a well-known story about him.
ask him whether he reads the Qur'an.
list his virtues one by one.
games.why: she asked him, don't you read the Qur'an? when he said yes, she told him his character was the Qur'an. she pointed him to a book he already had.

practice: Choose one of his habits: helping at home without being asked, holding back the sigh when someone gets something wrong, or a real smile for someone you'll see today.

Picture where it happens, which room, which person, and walk through that moment once in your mind, doing it. If you pray, you can send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, as Muslims do; if not, simply keep the picture of that one moment.

wordCard.voice: Khuluq, the Prophet's character and disposition, which Aisha said was simply the Qur'an lived out. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: character, disposition. the word in Aisha's answer and in the Qur'an's description of him.

carryVoice: Your line: his character was the qur'an. A whole life, learned one habit at a time. See you tomorrow.
